ops.name: build.array
ops.summary: Repeat an object along a vector, or in a 2D/3D grid. Fences, columns, pipes, city blocks, crowd props.

counts.description: Repeat count per axis, e.g. [5] or [4,4] or [3,3,2]

join.description: Merge into a single mesh (fewer draw calls)

ops.name: build.bevel
ops.summary: Chamfer an object's sharp edges. The single highest-impact polish step for hard-surface props.

angle.description: Only bevel edges sharper than this (degrees)

ops.name: build.box
ops.summary: Chamfered box. The chamfer is what makes a box read as a solid object under game lighting instead of a flat card.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

smooth.description: Smooth shading with a sharp-edge threshold

bevel_segments.description: Chamfer resolution (2 is plenty for game assets)

ops.name: build.cleanup
ops.summary: Weld duplicate vertices and optionally dissolve coplanar faces. Run before measuring or exporting.

dissolve_flat.description: Merge coplanar faces (cuts triangles, can create n-gons)

ops.name: build.cylinder
ops.summary: Cylinder, cone or truncated cone (set radius_top). Pillars, pipes, barrels, tent poles.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

smooth.description: Smooth shading (usually right for round shapes)

radius_top.description: Top radius; -1 means same as bottom, 0 makes a cone

segments.description: Radial segments — 12-16 is the game-asset sweet spot

ops.name: build.deform
ops.summary: Taper, twist or noise-displace a mesh. Turns generic primitives into things with character.

amount.description: taper: top scale factor. noise/jitter: displacement in metres. squash: Z scale

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: build.extrude
ops.summary: Inset-and-extrude faces selected by their normal direction. Makes panels, ledges, windows and recesses.

inset.description: Inset before extruding — this is what makes a panel not a spike

threshold.description: Normal alignment required to count as facing that direction

ops.name: build.greeble
ops.summary: Scatter panel detail across faces — sci-fi hulls, machinery, city blocks, tech walls. Deterministic for a given seed.

seed.description: Random seed; same seed gives the same result forever

density.description: Fraction of faces that get a panel (0..1)

cuts.description: Subdivision passes before panelling — more cuts, finer greeble

ops.name: build.lathe
ops.summary: Revolve a 2D profile into a solid. The highest value-per-parameter op here: bottles, vases, columns, goblets, chess pieces, tree trunks, fountains.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

profile.description: Flat [radius0, height0, radius1, height1, ...] pairs, bottom to top

ops.name: build.mirror
ops.summary: Mirror geometry across an axis. Halves the modelling work for anything symmetrical — characters, vehicles, buildings.

ops.name: build.plane
ops.summary: Flat quad, optionally grid-subdivided. Floors, walls, water, billboards, terrain bases.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

smooth.description: Smooth shading with a sharp-edge threshold

ops.name: build.prism
ops.summary: N-sided prism. Hex tiles, crystals, columns, low-poly trunks.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

smooth.description: Smooth shading with a sharp-edge threshold

ops.name: build.sphere
ops.summary: UV sphere or icosphere. Icospheres have even topology and are better bases for rocks and organic shapes.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

ops.name: build.subdivide
ops.summary: Subdivide all faces. Use sparingly — subdivision multiplies triangles fast.

ops.name: build.sweep
ops.summary: Sweep a 2D cross-section along a path — the workhorse for level geometry. Racetracks, grandstands, roads, ramparts, rails, tunnels, mouldings and pipes are all one profile plus one path. Frames use parallel transport, so a closed loop does not twist.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

profile.description: Flat [lateral0, vertical0, lateral1, vertical1, ...] cross-section in metres, relative to the path

path.description: Flat [x0,y0,z0, x1,y1,z1, ...] path points; leave empty and use path_shape instead

straight.description: oval: length of each straight in metres

length.description: line: total length in metres along X

segments.description: Path resolution (per turn for an oval)

closed_path.description: Close the path into a loop (oval and circle are always closed)

closed_profile.description: Treat the cross-section as a closed outline (a solid tube) rather than an open strip

ops.name: build.torus
ops.summary: Torus. Rings, handles, hoops, portal frames.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

ops.name: build.wedge
ops.summary: Right-triangle prism. Ramps, roof sections, chamfer blockouts.

material.description: Material preset name, or '' for none. See meta.palette

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile for box projection

smooth.description: Smooth shading with a sharp-edge threshold

ops.name: char.animate
ops.summary: Author a keyframed animation clip on a rig: idle, walk, run, attack, jump, death or wave. Real pose-to-pose keys at contact/passing frames, not sine-wave wiggle — the difference between a walk and a shuffle.

length.description: Clip length in frames (24 frames at 30 fps = 0.8 s)

amplitude.description: Motion scale — 0.6 is subtle, 1.4 is exaggerated

loop.description: Match the last frame to the first so the clip cycles

action_name.description: Action name (defaults to the clip name)

ops.name: char.attach
ops.summary: Parent a prop to a character bone — a sword to hand_r, a shield to hand_l, a helmet to head. Keeps the prop's own pivot, so it animates with the character.

ops.name: char.humanoid
ops.summary: Proportioned humanoid blockout using classic figure-drawing head ratios (7.5 realistic, 8 heroic, 4 chibi). ~1400 tris. Pair with char.rig and char.animate for a complete animated character.

detail.description: Limb cross-section segments (6-10 is the game range)

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: char.pose
ops.summary: Set a static pose on a rig — T-pose, A-pose, sitting, or a custom per-bone rotation. Useful for reference renders and for fixing an import rest pose.

bones.description: custom only: {"bone_name": [rx, ry, rz], ...} in degrees

ops.name: char.rig
ops.summary: Build a humanoid armature fitted to a mesh and skin it with distance-falloff weights. Single 'hips' root, snake_case bone names, glTF/Godot-compatible. No GUI needed.

height.description: Character height; 0 measures it from the mesh bounds

build.description: Proportions the rig assumes — match char.humanoid

falloff.description: Weight blend sharpness; higher is more rigid

ops.name: check.asset
ops.summary: Run the studio's ADR 0006 asset rules against the open scene: naming, units, applied transforms, origins, UVs, budgets, bone conventions, collision, textures, glTF-safe shaders. Same checks as `just asset-validate`, but before you write the file.

ops.name: check.critique
ops.summary: Quality critique with specific, actionable findings: triangle-density hot spots, degenerate and n-gon faces, UV stretch, texel-density mismatch between objects, non-manifold edges, unused material slots. Pair it with render.contact_sheet — numbers plus eyes.

texture_size.description: Texture resolution the texel-density figures assume

ops.name: check.silhouette
ops.summary: Score how readable an object's silhouette is from the standard game camera angles. A prop that fails here will not read at gameplay distance no matter how good its texture is.

samples.description: Rays per axis for the projected-area estimate

ops.name: env.arena
ops.summary: Complete combat arena in one call: floor, tiered walls, entrance arches and corner towers. A whole playable space from a single op.

tiers.description: Spectator tiers stepping up behind the wall

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: env.cliff
ops.summary: Rock cliff wall or canyon face with stratified layers. Blocks sightlines and frames a play space without the cost of terrain.

strata.description: How pronounced the rock layering is

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: env.road
ops.summary: Road, path or river bed following a polyline, conformed to a terrain surface if given.

target.description: Terrain to drape onto (empty = flat at Z=0)

offset.description: Height above the surface, to avoid z-fighting

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: env.scatter
ops.summary: Scatter copies of an object over a surface with Poisson-ish spacing, aligned to the surface normal. The op that turns bare terrain into a forest, a rockfield or a graveyard.

target.description: Surface to scatter onto (empty = scatter on the Z=0 plane)

area.description: Scatter area in metres when there is no target

align_to_normal.description: 0 = always upright, 1 = fully follow the surface tilt

seed.description: Random seed

join.description: Merge into one mesh — critical for draw calls

ops.name: env.terrain
ops.summary: Heightfield terrain with fBm noise, optional plateaus and erosion-like smoothing. Deterministic across machines, so CI can regenerate and diff it.

scale.description: Noise frequency — lower is broader hills

flatten_center.description: Radius in metres of a flat buildable area at the origin

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: env.water
ops.summary: Water plane with a gentle wave mesh and a translucent material. Fills moats, lakes and canals.

level.description: Z height of the water surface

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: export.asset
ops.summary: One call: save the .blend master, export the GLB, write the .meta.json sidecar and render a contact sheet. The complete hand-off for a finished asset.

asset_id.description: snake_case asset identifier — names every output file

out_dir.description: Directory for the outputs (defaults to the session output dir)

ai_prompt.description: What the asset was asked for — recorded in provenance

contact_sheet.description: Also render a review contact sheet

strict.description: Block export on problems that would corrupt the import

ops.name: export.blend
ops.summary: Save the .blend master. Under ADR 0006 the .blend is the committed source of truth and the GLB is a derived artefact — always save both.

ops.name: export.gltf
ops.summary: Export to GLB/glTF with an engine-specific preset. Checks for the things that silently break an import first — unapplied scale, missing UVs, procedural materials — and tells you rather than shipping a broken file.

format.description: Binary GLB (one file) or text glTF (separate assets)

draco.description: Draco mesh compression — smaller files, slower load, not all importers support it

strict.description: Fail on problems that would corrupt the import instead of warning

ops.name: export.meta
ops.summary: Write the .meta.json sidecar the studio asset pipeline requires — id, licence, provenance including AI-generation disclosure, budgets and policies. Without this, `just asset-validate` rejects the asset.

ai_tool.description: AI tool used — required for honest provenance

ai_model.description: Model that drove the generation, if any

ai_prompt.description: Prompt or intent that produced the asset

ops.name: gameready.atlas
ops.summary: Merge several objects into one mesh with one shared material and a repacked UV atlas. The most effective draw-call reduction available — a room of 20 props becomes 1 draw call.

material.description: Material preset for the merged result

ops.name: gameready.budget
ops.summary: Check the scene against a platform triangle/texture budget and say what to do about anything over. Run this before export, every time.

asset_class.description: What kind of asset this is

objects.description: Objects to check (empty = every mesh in the scene)

ops.name: gameready.collision
ops.summary: Generate a physics collision proxy. Convex hulls are what you want for anything a character walks into; box is cheapest; simplified trimesh is for concave shapes like arenas and rooms. Named <object>-convcol / <object>-col per the studio import convention.

ratio.description: simplified only: decimation ratio for the trimesh proxy

inflate.description: Grow the proxy by this many metres (stops geometry poking through)

ops.name: gameready.lod
ops.summary: Generate a level-of-detail chain by decimation. Ratios are chosen so each level roughly halves the triangle count, which is what LOD switching expects. Named <object>_lod1..N to match the studio import convention.

levels.description: Number of reduced levels to create

ratios.description: Explicit decimation ratios, e.g. [0.5, 0.25, 0.1]. Empty auto-generates

layout.description: Offset each LOD along X for side-by-side review

ops.name: gameready.optimize
ops.summary: One-call cleanup pass: weld doubles, drop degenerate faces, recalculate normals, and report what it saved. Safe to run on anything.

dissolve_flat.description: Merge coplanar faces — cuts triangles but can create n-gons

triangulate.description: Triangulate (engines do this anyway; useful for exact counts)

ops.name: gameready.pivot
ops.summary: Fix pivots and transforms across many objects at once — the two things engines get wrong on import and nobody notices until a prop spins about its ankle.

apply_transforms.description: Bake rotation and scale into the mesh

snap_to_ground.description: Move each object so its lowest point sits at Z=0

to_origin.description: Also move the object itself to (0,0,0). Required for a single-asset master file — the studio validator rejects a root object that is not at the world origin

ops.name: gameready.socket
ops.summary: Add a named empty as an attachment socket — muzzle points, hardpoints, spawn markers, VFX anchors. Engines import empties as nodes you can query by name.

parent.description: Object to parent the socket to

ops.name: kit.piece
ops.summary: One modular kit piece with its origin at the grid corner, ready to snap. Build a whole set with kit.set instead if you want more than one.

grid.description: Grid module size in metres — use ONE value across the whole kit

uv_scale.description: Metres per UV tile — MUST match across the kit

detail.description: Extra edge loops for later greebling

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: kit.room
ops.summary: Assemble a closed room from kit pieces: floor, four walls with a door and windows, optional pillars and roof. Produces a playable space, not just parts.

size.description: Room size in grid modules [x, y]

doors.description: Number of doorway modules to cut into the walls

join.description: Merge into one mesh (recommended — one draw call)

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: kit.set
ops.summary: Generate a complete, texel-consistent modular kit in one call — floor, walls, door, window, corner, pillar, stairs, roof. This is the fastest path from nothing to a level a designer can actually build with.

uv_scale.description: Shared metres-per-UV-tile across the whole set

layout.description: Lay the pieces out in a row for review rendering

seed.description: Random seed

ops.name: material.bake
ops.summary: Bake procedural shading down to an image texture and rewire the material to use it. This is what makes procedural materials shippable.

samples.description: Cycles samples; 16 is plenty for base colour, raise for AO

unwrap.description: Auto-unwrap first — baking needs non-overlapping UVs

rewire.description: Replace the procedural graph with the baked texture

ops.name: material.consolidate
ops.summary: Merge materials that render identically into one shared material. Composing a scene from many prop recipes leaves a pile of near-duplicate materials, and every distinct material is a draw call — this collapses them without changing how anything looks.

tolerance.description: How close two materials' colour/roughness/metallic must be to count as the same

objects.description: Limit to these objects (empty = whole scene)

dry_run.description: Report what would merge without changing anything

ops.name: material.face_assign
ops.summary: Give a subset of faces its own material — trim strips, emissive panels, painted details. Selected by world-space direction or height.

preset.description: Material preset for the selected faces

band_min.description: top_band/bottom_band: lower bound as a fraction of height

band_max.description: top_band/bottom_band: upper bound as a fraction of height

ops.name: material.list
ops.summary: List materials in the file and flag any that glTF cannot export.

ops.name: material.procedural
ops.summary: Build a noise/voronoi/wave/gradient material. Gives surfaces real variation instead of flat colour — but it must be baked (material.bake) before it can export to glTF.

kind.description: Pattern type: noise=rock/dirt, voronoi=cracked stone/scales, wave=wood grain/strata, gradient=vertical fade, checker=UV debug

roughness.description: Base roughness; the pattern modulates around it

distortion.description: Warps the pattern; makes wood grain and marble believable

ops.name: material.set
ops.summary: Create and assign a PBR material. Prefer a preset name (stone, wood, metal, gold, crystal...) — the presets have physically sane roughness/metallic values.

preset.description: Material preset; see meta.palette for the list

roughness.description: Override roughness 0..1; -1 keeps the preset value

metallic.description: Override metallic 0..1; -1 keeps the preset value

emission.description: Emission strength; -1 keeps the preset value

ops.name: meta.help
ops.summary: Full parameter schema and defaults for one operation.

ops.name: meta.ops
ops.summary: List every available operation with its parameters. Call this first if you are unsure what exists.

tag.description: Filter by tag (session, build, prop, kit, env, char, gameready, render, export, check)

search.description: Filter by substring in the op name or summary

detail.description: How much to return per op

ops.name: meta.palette
ops.summary: The studio colour palette and material presets. Use these names instead of inventing colours — palette discipline is what makes a set of assets look like one game.

ops.name: object.delete
ops.summary: Remove objects from the scene.

ops.name: object.duplicate
ops.summary: Copy an object, optionally placing the copy in one call.

new_name.description: Name for the copy (auto-derived when empty)

ops.name: object.inspect
ops.summary: Detailed report for one object: topology, UV quality, texel density, materials, bounds.

texture_size.description: Texture resolution used for the texel-density figure

ops.name: object.join
ops.summary: Merge several meshes into one object, de-duplicating material slots. Fewer objects means fewer draw calls.

names.description: Objects to merge (the first one's transform wins)

ops.name: object.list
ops.summary: List object names in the scene, optionally filtered by a name prefix.

prefix.description: Only return names starting with this

ops.name: object.origin
ops.summary: Set an object's pivot. Use 'bottom' for floor props, 'center' for pickups, 'world' for modular kit pieces.

ops.name: object.rename
ops.summary: Rename an object, coercing the new name to the studio's snake_case convention.

ops.name: object.shade
ops.summary: Set smooth or flat shading. Smooth shading with an angle threshold is what makes curved props read as curved.

angle.description: Edges sharper than this angle (degrees) stay hard

ops.name: object.transform
ops.summary: Move, rotate or scale an object. Rotation is in degrees.

apply.description: Bake rotation+scale into mesh data (required before export)

ops.name: prop.banner
ops.summary: Hanging banner or flag with a cloth wave. ~180 tris. Cheap way to add faction identity and colour to grey architecture.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

size.description: Cloth width and drop in metres

ops.name: prop.barrel
ops.summary: Lathed barrel with a belly and iron bands. ~500 tris. Bands get their own material slot so they can read as metal.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

belly.description: How much the middle bulges (0 = straight cylinder)

open_top.description: Hollow out the top (for water butts, planters)

ops.name: prop.chest
ops.summary: Treasure chest with a curved lid, iron banding and a lock plate. ~700 tris. Lid is a separate object so it can be hinged and animated.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

size.description: Base dimensions (lid adds height on top)

separate_lid.description: Keep the lid as its own object for hinge animation

ops.name: prop.crate
ops.summary: Wooden crate with a recessed-panel frame. ~350 tris. The frame is what makes it read as a crate rather than a box.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

planks.description: Horizontal plank divisions per panel (0 for plain)

ops.name: prop.crystal
ops.summary: Crystal cluster: several tapered prisms fanned from a common base. ~300 tris. Emissive by default — reads as a light source and a landmark.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

spread.description: Maximum lean from vertical, in degrees

ops.name: prop.debris
ops.summary: Scattered rubble field: broken stone, planks and dust chunks around a point. ~50 tris per piece. Turns a clean floor into a fought-over one.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

ops.name: prop.fence
ops.summary: Fence run with posts and rails. ~40 tris per metre. Blocks player movement and sells scale better than almost any other cheap prop.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

ops.name: prop.furniture
ops.summary: Table, bench, stool, shelf or bed frame. ~200 tris. The set dressing that makes an interior look inhabited.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

ops.name: prop.pillar
ops.summary: Classical column: base, tapered shaft, capital, optional fluting. ~600 tris. Instant architecture.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

ops.name: prop.rock
ops.summary: Irregular rock with a flat base so it sits on the ground instead of floating. ~200 tris at detail 2. The single most reused environment prop in any game.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

flatten_base.description: Cut a flat bottom so it beds into terrain

ops.name: prop.sack
ops.summary: Cloth sack, cinched at the neck. ~400 tris. Good filler for markets, camps and storerooms.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

slump.description: How much the body sags and spreads at the base

ops.name: prop.torch
ops.summary: Wall torch or standing brazier with an emissive flame. ~250 tris. Emissive props double as level-design landmarks.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

ops.name: prop.tree
ops.summary: Stylised low-poly tree: tapered trunk plus layered canopy. ~450 tris. Canopy is a separate material slot so it can take a foliage/alpha shader.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

lean.description: Trunk lean in degrees — a perfectly vertical tree looks fake

ops.name: prop.weapon
ops.summary: Sword, axe, spear, hammer or shield built from a blade/haft/grip breakdown. ~400 tris. Pivot sits at the grip so it parents straight to a hand bone.

name.description: Object name (defaults to the recipe name)

seed.description: Random seed — same seed always gives the same asset

ops.name: render.camera
ops.summary: Render from an explicit camera position and target. Auto-framing always fits the WHOLE subject, which is useless on a 700 m stadium or a 40 m terrain — this is how you get a close-up, an eye-level gameplay view, or a hero shot.

lens.description: Focal length in mm — 24 is wide, 50 neutral, 105 compressed

aspect.description: Width / height. Use 1.78 for a 16:9 gameplay framing

light_distance.description: Light rig scale in metres; 0 fits it to the whole scene

ops.name: render.contact_sheet
ops.summary: THE review image. Renders hero/front/side/top plus a wireframe pass (shows topology and wasted triangles) and a checker pass (shows UV stretch and texel-density mismatches), composited into one PNG. Look at this after generating anything — it is how you catch problems a triangle count cannot show.

ops.name: render.turntable
ops.summary: Render an orbit of frames around the subject. Use when a single angle cannot settle whether a silhouette works.

ops.name: render.view
ops.summary: Render one framed view of the scene or of specific objects. The camera and a three-point light rig are auto-fitted to the subject, so you never get an empty or blown-out frame.

objects.description: Objects to frame and show (empty = whole scene)

samples.description: Render samples — 24 is enough to judge form

engine.description: Render engine. 'auto' means Cycles/CPU, which is the only one that works without a GPU context; 'eevee' is faster but crashes headless on machines with no display server

ops.name: session.import
ops.summary: Import an existing glTF/GLB, OBJ, FBX or .blend into the current scene. Use this to inspect, critique, fix or extend assets a game already ships — not just ones you generated.

prefix.description: Rename imported objects with this prefix (keeps names snake_case)

location.description: Offset to place the import at

ops.name: session.info
ops.summary: Full scene report: every object with triangle counts, materials, UVs and bounds. Cheap; call it often.

ops.name: session.open
ops.summary: Load an existing .blend so you can inspect, fix or extend an asset instead of rebuilding it.

ops.name: session.reset
ops.summary: Clear the scene to a deterministic empty metric-unit state. Start every new asset with this.

unit_scale.description: Blender unit scale; keep 1.0 = 1 metre for game engines

ops.name: session.restore
ops.summary: Roll the scene back to a snapshot taken earlier in this session.

ops.name: session.save
ops.summary: Write the scene to a .blend master file (the committed source of truth in ADR 0006).

path.description: Output .blend path; relative paths land under the output dir

ops.name: session.snapshot
ops.summary: Save an in-memory scene checkpoint you can roll back to. Take one before any risky or destructive edit.

ops.name: uv.lightmap
ops.summary: Add a second, non-overlapping UV channel for baked lighting. Godot and Unity both require this for static lightmaps.

name.description: Name of the new UV layer

margin.description: Island padding — lightmaps need more than base textures

ops.name: uv.normalize
ops.summary: Fit existing UVs into the 0..1 square, preserving proportions.

ops.name: uv.pack
ops.summary: Repack existing UV islands into 0..1 without re-unwrapping. Use after joining objects or editing seams.

ops.name: uv.report
ops.summary: Measure UV quality: texel density, coverage, island count, overlap. Texel density is the number to match across an asset set — mismatched density is the most common reason AI-made assets look wrong together.

texture_size.description: Texture resolution the density figure assumes

ops.name: uv.unwrap
ops.summary: Generate UVs. Use 'box' with a shared uv_scale for anything using a tiling or trim texture (keeps texel density uniform across a whole kit); use 'smart_packed' for props that need their own baked texture.

scale.description: box only: metres per UV tile. Use the SAME value across a kit

margin.description: smart only: island padding, prevents bleed at low mip levels
